description: brgen language feature ledger schema. The ledger declares that a feature exists and gives it a stable identifier; it does NOT record which backends support it. Support is measured, not declared - see rebrgen/docs/draft/ast_prototype_analysis.md for why. Entries are split by kind into what the language has and what the toolchain does.

note.description: Free-text note about the ledger itself

features.description: The features. Order is not significant; id is the identity.

id.description: Stable identifier. Never reused, even if the feature is removed - a gap is expected.

slug.description: Readable identifier. Referenced as <id>-<slug>, e.g. F0034-trial-match, matching the docs/decisions/ ADR convention.

kind.description: Whether a format author has to know this to write .bgn (language), or it is something the toolchain does or derives on its own (toolchain). Orthogonal to category - a toolchain entry still lives in some layer.

category.description: Which layer of the language the feature lives in. lexical is token shapes only; grammar-level rules that are not tied to one construct (statement separation, indent blocks) are syntax. Categories group; they carry no semantics.

summary.description: One or two sentences on what the feature is

covers.description: Repository-relative paths of .bgn inputs exercising this feature. Many-to-many: one file may cover several features and one feature may span several files. An empty array means the feature has no dedicated input yet - that gap is the point of recording it.

notes.description: Known limits, partial implementations, or pointers to an ADR. Only record what a file or document already states - do not put guesses here.
